title: Do not scale apparent ROAS growth when contribution profit deteriorates
scenario: Attributed sales and ROAS improved after a price discount and heavier ad exposure, but unit economics worsened. The campaign now produces more attributed revenue while contribution profit after ads is materially lower and close to zero.

forbidden_behaviors: Recommend scaling solely because ROAS and attributed revenue improved.
Call the current state more profitable without using contribution economics.
Ignore the price/discount-driven deterioration in contribution after ads.
required_observations: ROAS improved while profit after ads fell materially.
Revenue efficiency and business profitability can move in opposite directions.
Scaling should be gated by marginal contribution and the declared business objective, not ROAS alone.

rubric.requirement: Separate attributed revenue efficiency from contribution economics.
Use the supplied cost and discount context instead of relying on ROAS alone.
Block automatic scaling when incremental revenue has weak or deteriorating contribution profit.
State what additional marginal-profit evidence would justify a future scale decision.
